subject: Starlite Health - Security onboarding: SIG path & dataflow questions
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alice Burke <alice.burke@starlitehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Starlite Health - Security onboarding: SIG path & dataflow questions

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the demo today — really appreciate the time and the clarity on Starlite's ingestion patterns. Per our discussion, I wanted to recap the security/compliance items we flagged and propose next steps so we can scope the vendor questionnaire (SIG vs CAIQ vs custom).

Quick recap / asks from Redwood:
- SOC 2: You indicated Starlite requires SOC 2 evidence for vendor onboarding. Do you need the full report or will an SOC 2 Type II summary + control mapping suffice for initial review?
- Data residency: Confirming EU data residency is not required for this pilot, right? (You mentioned US-only for now.)
- Regulated data: You flagged potential PHI in some workflows. Can you confirm which API flows will touch PHI (write a short list of endpoints or product features)?
- Questionnaire path: We can do a SIG Prefill (fastest), a CAIQ, or your custom XLS. Which does your security team prefer? If SIG prefill is OK, please share the primary security contact and any required SLA/pricing constraints.

Proposed next steps:
1) If SIG prefill: I’ll send our prefilled workbook + SOC 2 summary (attached) and a short mapping to your controls by EOD tomorrow.
2) If custom questionnaire: please send the template and I’ll route to our security team for completion — ETA 3–5 business days for initial pass.
3) If SOC 2 full report is required, procurement typically needs an NDA or limited distribution arrangement — flag if that’s the case.

Can you confirm preferred questionnaire path and share the best security contact (name + email)? Once we have that we’ll attach the prefill and a proposed evidence list (logs, KMS, network diagrams) so you can mark owners.

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Hi Camila —

Great to meet you yesterday — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers and clarifying questions from our security team: 

Answers from Starlite:
- SOC 2: Initially we accept the SOC 2 Type II summary + control mapping for vendor reviews; we reserve the right to request the full report for production contracts. For pilot authorization, summary + mapping is fine.
- Data residency: Correct — pilot is US-only. We will revisit EU residency for later phases.
- PHI: The only flows that may touch PHI are the patient-intake transcription pipeline and the secure messaging route (these are the two endpoints). We can provide a short list of API calls by EOD tomorrow.
- Questionnaire path: Security team prefers SIG prefill first — it's fastest for our procurement cadence.

Clarifying asks from Security (security@starlitehealth.com):
1) Can Redwood indicate whether KV cache is encrypted at rest and what KMS you use?
2) We need an explicit statement on key rotation cadence and whether HSM-backed KMS is available.
3) For SOC 2 evidence: what logs (retention windows and sample locations) can you provide for a 90-day sample?

Procurement copied to this thread (procurement@starlitehealth.com) asked about timing: they want the prefill + SOC summary to review by next Friday (2027-10-15).

If you can send the prefilled SIG and a proposed evidence checklist + timelines, we can route to procurement and security for the pilot.

Thanks —
Alice Burke
Director of Product Operations
Starlite Health

Camila —

Saw Alice's asks. Draft answers and artifacts below that we should send in the prefill. I grabbed the SOC 2 summary and a short evidence checklist (will attach the prefill template).

Suggested responses for the SIG prefill:
- KV cache encryption: Yes — all KV caches and disk-backed caches are encrypted at rest. We use AWS KMS (customer-managed KMS available on Redwood Private / Dedicated). For hosted: AWS KMS with AWS-managed keys by default; we can enable CMKs for dedicated customers.
- Key rotation & HSM: Default rotation is 365 days for service-managed keys; we support HSM-backed KMS via customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) on Private deployments. Note: rotation cadence can be documented in the control mapping; recommend noting CMK/HSM availability and that customer can request a rotation schedule in contract.
- Logs & retention: We can provide application request logs and audit trails. Typical retention windows: 90 days for request logs, 365 days for audit trails (longer retention available as an add-on). For a 90-day sample we can package redacted logs with time ranges and request IDs.

Attachments to include: 
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (already attached to camila's note)
- redwood-sig-prefill-template.xlsx (prefill with high-level responses; leave controls where we need input)
- evidence-checklist.txt (short list mapping owners: network diagrams, KMS config, log samples)

Timing: If Camila sends the prefill today, security/procurement can review and we should be able to get initial feedback by 2027-10-12 which meets procurement's desire to review by 10/15. If Starlite requests the full SOC 2 later, that adds a week for legal/NDA routing.

Let me know if you want me to complete any of the prefill rows directly (I can take the infra/ops controls).

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Alice / Starlite team —

Thanks for the quick answers and the timing note. Attached is our SIG prefill (redwood-sig-prefill-template.xlsx) with our initial responses and the SOC 2 summary (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf). I've also included a one-page evidence checklist and proposed owners. Highlights: 

- KV encryption: Confirmed encrypted at rest; CMK/HSM options available for Private/Dedicated.
- Key rotation: Default service-managed rotation = 365 days; CMK rotation cadence is customer-controlled.
- Logs: We can provide a 90-day sample of request logs and audit trails; we will redact PII/PHI/IDs per your guidance — please tell us which time windows and endpoints you want sampled.

Requesting next actions from Starlite: 
1) Confirm the preferred time window for a 90-day log sample and which endpoints (patient-intake transcription pipeline + secure messaging) to include.
2) Share the security contact full name and phone if we need a short technical call (we can cover KMS/HSM details).
3) Procurement: please confirm receipt and whether a limited-distribution NDA is required for the full SOC 2 report later.

If we get confirmation on the above by EOD tomorrow (10/07), Marissa can turn around any infra-specific rows in the prefill and we’ll send the packaged evidence for procurement/security review by Monday (10/11).

Thanks all — looking forward to moving this through.

Camila Reyes
